title: Mini-SDKs field trip labs and ops checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a tactical, low-friction kit for running 60–90 minute "field trip" labs with small teams (1–3 engineers) to validate SDK onboarding, failure modes, telemetry surface area, and quick UX fixes. Treat these as recurring micro-experiments that feed the larger SDK onramp backlog.

Why this exists (context):
- We ship many SDK changes and need a fast way to surface real integration pain points across languages and environments without a full formal usability study.
- Field trip labs are hands-on, short, and pragmatic: get a dev from zero to a simple integrated sample app, exercise fallbacks, capture telemetry gaps.

Audience:
- New SDK engineers (internal), solutions engineers, developer advocates, small customer engineering teams for early feedback.

Goals (what success looks like after a session):
- Developer completes quick sample app (hello-to-chat or embedder) in <45 minutes using local dev experience.
- Telemetry events for first API call, first error, and rollout fallback emitted and visible in Console traces.
- At least 2 concrete UX/SDK issues recorded as reproducible tickets (Jira/Linear).

Prereqs (pre-lab checklist, 10m prep):
- Participant has Git, Docker, and Node/Python/Go toolchain installed.
- Provide a disposable Redwood API key (redwood-dev-fieldtrip-*) or instructions to use a dev harness.
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/fieldtrip (branch stub) or local starter zip.
- devcontainer available? (yes recommended) — include a simple devcontainer.json that pre-installs CLI and auth helper.

Session template (90m recommended):
- 0–10m: Kickoff & goals, confirm prerequisites, explain telemetry targets to observe.
- 10–25m: Local environment spin-up (clone, install, configure key, run devcontainer if used).
- 25–50m: Wire sample app: 1 API call (generation) + 1 embedding flow + request streaming example.
- 50–65m: Chaos & fallbacks: simulate latency, drop token, switch to local stub, trigger quota errors.
- 65–80m: Observability & tracing: walk Console to find the trace, cost breakdown, and per-route metrics.
- 80–90m: Debrief: log tickets, quick fixes, and follow-ups. Decide which items go to triage.

Quick commands (examples used in the lab):
- Clone + install (node example):
  git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk.git && cd sdk/examples/node/quick-chat
  npm ci
- Run sample (env var pattern):
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood-dev-fieldtrip-abc123
  node quick-chat.js
- Curl smoke test (replace KEY):
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-mini-1","input":"Explain the field trip lab in two sentences."}'

Telemetry probes to validate (observable markers):
- event.sdk_first_start (contains sdk_version, runtime, language)
- event.api_call_initiated (model, route, client_id)
- event.kv_cache_hit (if applicable)
- event.error_unhandled (error_code, stack_snippet)
- trace.request.latency (tokenized breakdown)

Acceptance criteria for a successful mini-lab: (binary checks)
- Sample app runs end-to-end without manual code changes beyond inserting API key.
- At least one error condition was triggered and visible in Console with adequate context.
- Ticket recorded with reproducible steps, stack/console output, and severity.

Common failure modes & quick mitigations:
- Missing env vars / auth: provide a tiny auth helper script that writes a .redwoodrc and a fallback message for 401s.
- Blocking firewall in corp networks: instruct ranters to use proxy or devcontainer w/ preconfigured egress.
- Long cold-start times: show 'simulated latency' script rather than waiting for infra autoscale; capture trace anyway.

Suggested instrument changes (top-of-list items we expect to come from labs):
- Add sdk_first_start event to all language SDKs with install-time metadata.
- Surface per-token cost estimate in sample app logs for quick cost signal.
- Add a minimal error envelope to all error responses with stable error_key for triage.

Ticket template (copy-paste into Jira/Linear):
- Title: [field-lab] <short description>
- Steps to reproduce: exact commands + env + small code snippet
- Observed: console output / screenshot (link)
- Expected: what we expected to see
- Severity: high/medium/low
- Suggested owner: eng-developer-experience or eng-serving-runtime

Post-lab ops checklist (what to do after the session):
- File one reproducible ticket per unique issue. Tag with "field-lab" and team owner.
- Add telemetry gaps to the instrumentation backlog (label: telemetry-gap).
- If a small doc/FAQ would have prevented the delay, write a 1-paragraph blurb and add to SDK README.
- If a reproducible bug, create PR template with test case attached; assign to on-call in serving-runtime.

Example prompts and test vectors to include in the starter repo (short list):
- Regression detection: "Summarize the following product note in 30 words." (checks generation quality + token length)
- Safety edge: "Produce a list of operational troubleshooting steps for an API 503." (checks safety/hallucination)
- Embedding stability: Provide 3 semantically-similar sentences and expect cosine similarity ranking high.

Retention & scaling: running these weekly with rotating dev advocates helps build a backlog of real-world friction. Aim for 6 labs/month across languages (Node, Python, Go, Java).

Low-effort artifacts to ship after a successful run:
- One-sentence changelog entry for SDK release notes describing improvement or fix.
- 1-paragraph add to README showing the exact commands used in the lab.
- A minimal recorded screencap (3–5 min) showing the Console trace and the sample app run.

Notes to self (scavenged hacks we've used):
- Keep a small dev credentials pool and rotate monthly; makes repros faster than provisioning tokens ad-hoc.
- Ship a tiny stub server in examples that can emulate 401/429/503 without touching production quotas.
- Use a single Linear board column called "field-lab triage" for quick visibility.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we make the field-trip branch a protected sandbox with seeded test data? (pros/cons)
- How aggressive should the telemetry schema be across SDKs to avoid endless churn? propose a quarterly schema lock.

References & anchors:
- ENG-2381 (Confluence experiment brief) — see linked_artifacts above.
- Example PR with devcontainer + auth helper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/612
- Suggested Linear backlog lane: LD-1123

If you run a lab, drop short notes in #devexp-field-labs Slack channel and ping me (Aisha). I’ll consolidate and push high-priority items into the weekly SDK grooming cadence.
